newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures rally after drop in retail sales.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures rally after drop in retail sales.

text.p: U.S. debt futures rallied after an unexpected drop in U.S. May retail sales.
It was third consecutive monthly retail sales decline.
May sales fell 0.1 percent both overall and excluding autos, and April's figures were revised downward to show an 0.9-percent drop overall and an 0.5-percent decline excluding autos.
September Treasury bond futures broke above resistance near 111-00 and charged to the highest price since late February after the report.
Fast market conditions were seen on the rally.
A Reuters poll of economists had shown an average May estimate of up 0.4 percent overall and up 0.3 percent excluding autos.

"Everything went fast market right after the number," a Eurodollar trader said. "But the revision is what really got you here," he added. "Down 0.9 percent in April -- that's huge. For right now retail sales tell me that the Fed's on hold," he said.
About 15 minutes after the data Eurodollar contracts began coming off fast market status, but trade remained very active, the Euro trader said.
"These are very bullish numbers," a Treasury bond futures trader said, calling floor trade "crazy."
Still, he said there was a big seller somewhere between 111-08/32 and 111-15/32 that was keeping a lid on gains for now.
"We'll work through that and then there's 111-16/32 channel resistance (and) next stop 112-00," he said.
December Euros poked above resistance at 93.88 to hit 93.89, but scaled back from the highs slightly in the minutes after the data. Trading there was still very active, floor sources reported.
Also reported at 0730 CDT/1230 GMT were the latest weekly jobless claims, which rose to 339,000 in the June 7 week from 338,000 in the prior week.

At 0801 CDT/1301 GMT, September T-bonds were up 20/32 at 111-7/32, 10-yr notes rose 12/32 to 108-16/32, munis rose 18/32 to 119-03/32, Sept bills were up 0.015 point at 94.750, and Dec Euros rose 0.065 to 93.880. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
